correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the disk geometry and checked the bound independently. The farthest center changes at the rays bisecting consecutive opposite-center directions. In one such sector the corner at radius r satisfies r sin(alpha)=sin(q/m) and t+r cos(alpha)=cos(q/m), where alpha=pi/m and q=P/2. This gives t=sin((pi-q)/m)/sin(alpha), strictly decreasing from 1 to 0. Summing the corner polygon and the unit circular segments gives the stated area profile. With s=(P-pi)/pi, beta=pi/2, and k=m/(2 sin(alpha)), the gap is cos(beta s)-k[cos(alpha s)-cos(alpha)]. Its derivative with respect to q is positive on 0<q<pi/2 by strict increase of sin(alpha z)/sin(beta z) for 0<z<1 (x cot(x) decreases), and symmetry supplies the other half. For an independent check of the sharp envelope, regard the gap as a function of x=s^2. The second derivative of cos(a sqrt(x)) is a/(4 x^(3/2)) times the integral from 0 to a sqrt(x) of t sin(t) dt. Bounding sin(t) between 2t/pi and t gives the gap a strictly positive second derivative, since 2 beta^4/pi>k alpha^4 (the latter is at most pi^4/36). Its chord between x=0 and 1 is therefore a strict upper bound in between. This proves all equality cases; endpoint continuity forces the constant even on the open perimeter interval. Substitution gives G_m, the optimizing radius and the Reuleaux triangle; tan(x)/x gives the monotone limit. The frozen finite script is corroboration, not the proof, and was inspected rather than run.
residual_risks: Only the regular unit-center polygon family and its continuous endpoints were audited; no arbitrary-center maximization is inferred.

value.rationale: The total gap between two canonical profiles has one optimizing perimeter for every disk count. The sharp estimate controls all perimeters at once and distinguishes global sharpness, which is forced by degenerate endpoints, from the local curvature at the interior maximizer. That is meaningful additional information beyond a known exact area formula or another finite comparison.
residual_risks: This value claim is specific to the regular family and makes no assertion of a general upper stability theorem for ball-convex bodies.
